## Historical audit: S0097, chunk 5 of 7

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/replay_s1_r1/M_initial/C1/replay_selection/commons_29206714/trajectory.jsonl`. Only the supplied chunk is visible.

**Inferred goal:** Reconstruct a reference image as a historic kitchen scene and improve its visual match. The visible instruction requests comparison against original anchors; the reference and renders themselves are not visible to this audit. [S0097, line 15, characters 419000–423475; student response, line 17]

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Prior render and guidance | Step 2 completed 16 samples, saved a PNG and blend file, and was reported usable. The subsequent prompt asked for at most two discrepancies, attention to camera versus local scale, openings, supports and finishes, and a complete program or selection. Steps 1 and 2 were listed as successful. This is visible guidance, not an identified teacher diagnosis or proof of teacher input. [line 15, characters 419000–423475] |
| Student exploration | The student session received paths for the reference and two renders, completed with no tool calls, and returned a program. It attributed apparently high counter/shelf lines to base proportions and an apparently edge-on wheel to azimuth. These are student observations and hypotheses, not independently verified image findings. [lines 16–17] |
| Executed revision | Step 3 executed the returned program: it scales the cabinet base vertically by 0.82, extends the upper group about the crown, transforms the china and winder, and calculates a winder-to-counter adjustment. It sets the wheel to −48° and a specified position. The comments also describe raising and shifting it, but the earlier program is not visible here, so the actual parameter changes relative to step 2 cannot be established. [student response, line 17; execute, line 18] |
| Scene checks | The code specifies multiple groups: architecture, cabinet, china, winder, wheel and spindle; colored finishes, decorative geometry and translucent glasses; doors turned about hinges; wheel rims, spokes and supports. It calculates intended support contact, but neither physical connections nor rendered contact are independently verified. No image texture maps are evident in this program. Camera, two area lights and ambient world are specified; no camera or lighting defect can be established without the images. [lines 17–18] |
| Validation and selection | Step 3 reports `ok: true`, no error, a completed 16-sample render, saved PNG and blend, and empty stderr. Two selection events name step 3. Assertions check positive scaling factors and member counts, not visual match or geometric contact. [execution_result, line 19; select events, lines 20–21] |

**Outcome:** Technical execution and selection are recorded; **final visual correctness is unknown**, not formal scene success or demonstrated algorithm failure. This was not an empty patch or a visible technical interruption. No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt, or adoption is evidenced in this chunk; the generic prompt’s instructions are visibly followed in part, but their provenance is unspecified.

**Lessons and uncertainty:** The transferable practice illustrated is to document a discrepancy, hypothesis, intended change and dependency risk, then distinguish render completion from visual validation. The base-height and wheel-azimuth diagnoses are task-specific, unresolved hypotheses. Changing both families in one execution also limits attribution. Whether the wheel opening became visible, the winder contacts the counter, finishes were preserved relative to the prior build, or step 3 better matches the reference remains unknown without the images and unseen history.
